lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Short run today. Three thousand feet, two zones, same rules as the big job. Dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 4. We promised Day 18. The spec-keeper has both permits. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That is the short run. Look at where the lines ended up against what we promised.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Office, inspector reports the crew never got it. Say again?

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at five-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Short run today. Three thousand feet, two zones, same rules as the big job. Dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 4. We promised Day 18. The spec-keeper has both permits. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That is the short run. Look at where the lines ended up against what we promised.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Office, inspector reports the crew never got it. Say again?

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at five-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Short run today. Three thousand feet, two zones, same rules as the big job. Dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 4. We promised Day 18. The spec-keeper has both permits. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That is the short run. Look at where the lines ended up against what we promised.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at five-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

lines.text: Short run today. Three thousand feet, two zones, same rules as the big job. Dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 4. We promised Day 18. The spec-keeper has both permits. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Short run today. Three thousand feet, two zones, same rules as the big job. Dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 4. We promised Day 18. The spec-keeper has both permits. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That is the short run. Look at where the lines ended up against what we promised.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Office, inspector reports the crew never got it. Say again?

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at five-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Short run today. Three thousand feet, two zones, same rules as the big job. Dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 4. We promised Day 18. The spec-keeper has both permits. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That is the short run. Look at where the lines ended up against what we promised.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Office, inspector reports the crew never got it. Say again?

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at five-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

lines.text: Short run today. Three thousand feet, two zones, same rules as the big job. Dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 4. We promised Day 18. The spec-keeper has both permits. Call me before you change anything.
